newsitem.title: USA: Arrow Air expands, adding new cities.
newsitem.headline: Arrow Air expands, adding new cities.

text.p: Arrow Air Inc, the Miami-based all-cargo airline, is adding aircraft and new routes in an expansion push, its president said Wednesday.
"Our second L-1011 has been on for about two weeks and the third will be on our certificate in about 10 days," Jon Batchelor, president and chief operating officer, told Reuters.
Arrow, which also operates six Douglas DC-8 aircraft, added flights to Ciudad del Este and Asuncion, Paraguay several weeks ago.
"We are flying a minimum of three times a week," Batchelor said.
Freight going into Paraguay is computers and electronics and the flight coming back stops in Ecuador for flowers, fruits and vegetables, Batchelor said.
Arrow had planned to add flights to Venezuela, but that was contingent on landing rights in Colombia. The Colombian government rejected the application, Batchelor said.
Arrow also is considering adding Montevideo, Uruguay and La Paz and Santa Cruz, Bolivia, Batchelor said.
Arrow carried the sixth most freight through Miami International Airport in 1996, hauling 84,263 tons, an increase of 56 percent, according to statistics compiled by Dade County Aviation Department.
Arrow is owned by privately-held International Air Leases Inc, of Hialeah, Florida.
